claim: The seven documents a participant or contributor reads first now name the product plane. GROUND.md and CANON.md were owner-accepted on 2026-08-24 and say what product Soveraeign is and what it undertakes; until this change none of AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, SOV.md, README.md, .cursorrules or bindings/sov/profile.json mentioned either, so every launched agent read a nine-document governing set and never learned the product plane existed.

subject.artifact: the entry-point document set: AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, SOV.md, README.md, .cursorrules, bindings/sov/profile.json

visible_result.shows: Five commits. On main, AGENTS.md names GROUND.md zero times; on the branch it names it four times and states the two groups. The diff shows the Design System of Record split into what the product is and what this phase must prove, with AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md placed in neither as documents that govern participants and own no product claim. The last command shows 33 files on main already referencing the product plane, including six of the seven SERVICE-GROUND.md files under services/. Everything downstream knew; only the entry points did not.
visible_result.expect: 0 from the main grep, 4 from the branch grep, and 33 from the last command.

evidence.says: Status OWNER-ACCEPTED 2026-08-24, revision GROUND-1, rendering GROUND-1.1. Sixteen claims saying what product Soveraeign is. Its closing line reads: No governing document was modified to accommodate this.
Status OWNER-ACCEPTED 2026-08-24, CANON-3. Who a node is for, what Soveraeign undertakes, and the principal journeys an undertaking is reached by.

product_ground_status OWNER_ACCEPTED_EPOCH_1_GROUND_1 and product_canon_status OWNER_ACCEPTED_CANON_3_PROMISE_13_AND_14_RETIRED. The acceptance is recorded on a third surface, not only in the two documents themselves.

The owner ruling that accepted the ground, typed OWNER-RULED and APPLIED. The acceptances are its rulings 1 and 2, and it records that contracts/product-ground.json carries the acceptance by exact revision.

Supersedes decisions/0050 and takes the aggregate wall clock out of the exit code. README.md, scripts/verify.py and scripts/tests/test_verify_clocks.py all still cited 0050 and described a gate that fails past fifteen seconds. It also asserts the thirty-second ceiling is deliberately unreachable by load, which three witnesses have now defeated by observation.

grade() returns None past the slowest band and wall_clock_line() emits DEBT; the aggregate wall time never reaches the exit code. This is the independent path that proves the old docstrings wrong. Its line 8 carries the same unreachable-by-load rationale decisions/0081 does.
Seam S28 records that GROUND.md closing sentence is ambiguous in scope and reads falsely about the tree after this change, and that two of its three readings need an owner act.

why_it_matters: A launched agent does not carry an interactive session's context. It reads AGENTS.md, and AGENTS.md was its whole map of what governs this repository. The product plane has been owner-accepted for four days and is wired into 33 files on main - the contracts, the decision records, six of the seven SERVICE-GROUND.md files - so every agent has been working downstream of claims it was never told about, and answering product questions from PRD.md and SPEC.md, which own the phase and not the product. GROUND.md recorded the cause in its own closing sentence and nothing acted on it. The second half matters as much: the change states plainly that AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md govern participants and own no product claim, which is the line that stops this repository's internal working rules from being read as things Soveraeign promises the people who use a node.
what_could_defeat_it: The phrase owns no product claim could be equivocation rather than a real distinction. A first witness refused the earlier wording states no product claim as false, because GROUND.md grounds seven of its sixteen claims partly in named AGENTS.md sections and CANON.md grounds PROMISE-12 the same way. Two later independent witnesses re-tested the repaired wording against files this branch never touched, parsed the ground claims rather than counting by eye, and found the source-versus-ownership distinction is one GROUND.md and CANON.md already draw. If Bdo reads owns as an escape word anyway, the paragraph is still wrong.

Naming a third class of document - participant-conduct rules that own no product claim, in which a product rule may never be settled - is a new statement, not a restatement. A repository-wide search before this change returns nothing that says it. Two witnesses raised it independently. If Bdo judges that a new rule needs a decision record, this belongs in decisions/ and not in an entry point.

AGENTS.md mandatory pre-change reading list grew from ten documents to twelve, in a commit typed docs:. That changes every participant obligation on every consequential change. Two witnesses raised it as an owner question: acceptable as documentation, or does an obligation change want its own record?

Nothing enforces any of it. These are documentation edits. No check refuses a future entry point that drops the product plane again, and no check compares bindings/sov/profile.json governing_sources against the list AGENTS.md owns. The drift this closes can silently reopen.

The repo-law half of the separation is absent. decisions/0098 built a law registry so enforcement points resolve rules instead of re-reading prose, but contracts/law.json and scripts/sov_law.py are uncommitted on another session branch. An address in a governing document must resolve or verify refuses, so none of these documents can point at it yet. What is separated here is product from participant, not registry from prose.
residuals: Standing is BUILT and this packet claims nothing higher; witnessed_by is null deliberately. Four independent witnesses observed this branch and all four supported OPEN to BUILT. The first found a false sentence in the added paragraph, repaired in the third commit. The second found a commit message naming acceptance/A20.json before that file existed and under an identifier already held by the PRD rewrite on docs/prd-rewrite, and found the GROUND.md sentence recorded nowhere. The third found that the packet called that pointer closed when it was only counter-recorded, and that the counter-record doctrine in AGENTS.md governs the operational record rather than commit messages on an unpublished branch; the branch was rebuilt in response. The fourth supported BUILT to WITNESSED at commit ff7b46d and named three prose defects for repair in place: a residual saying ten readings while listing eleven, a stale witness count in seam S28, and a load-dependent budget figure stated as a fixed range. All three are repaired, so the tree presented here differs from the one the fourth witness attested by exactly those three corrections and nothing else. A fifth observation of that delta is what would carry WITNESSED to this tree.

The branch was rebuilt rather than annotated, after the third witness showed rewriting was permitted: AGENTS.md forbids rewriting published history and force-pushing a shared branch, and this branch has no upstream and no remote ref. The wrong acceptance/A20.json pointer is gone from every commit message rather than corrected in a later one, so nothing citing another concern's document reaches main. The pre-rewrite tip is preserved at refs/backup/plane-separation-pre-rewrite, commit bbf7b5f, and can be read to see exactly what was rewritten.

GROUND.md closing sentence, No governing document was modified to accommodate this, is ambiguous in scope: true about the 2026-08-24 acceptance act, false about the tree after this change. It is recorded as seam S28 rather than repaired, because two of the three readings require re-rendering an OWNER-ACCEPTED document from GROUND-1.1 to GROUND-1.2 or building a check that grades accepted documents for claims about the tree. The third reading needs nobody and closes the seam with a note. Bdo call.

The thirty-second catastrophic ceiling in the verification budget is reachable by host load, and as this packet is written it is holding the gate red. decisions/0081 asserts the ceiling is deliberately unreachable by load and that a check reaching thirty seconds has changed rather than been crowded; scripts/sovverify/budget.py line 8 says no host load explains it. Eleven readings of repository tooling tests on this branch, over bytes that changed no logic: 25.058, 25.538, 26.149, 27.91, 28.38, 28.924, 29.66, 33.616, 34.289, 39.047 and 40.228 seconds. The first seven exit 0; the last four exit 1 on the timing catastrophe with zero semantic failures and all 48 checks running. Three witnesses observed the flip independently and the builder then reproduced it four consecutive times while three sessions shared the host. The branch therefore does not currently pass scripts/verify.py, and the reason is the wall clock and nothing in the change. This is the false-rejection failure decisions/0081 was written to remove, arriving through the per-check ceiling it moved the pressure to. A fourth witness then ran an interleaved A/B against main at deb9a0f and measured the trunk itself red twice, at 31.753s and 30.732s, with no branch content involved, while the branch passed at 27.355s in the same series. grant:standing-landing-loop requires verify PASS, so on a loaded host no branch can reliably satisfy its own landing precondition and main cannot reliably satisfy it either. It is a finding against a decision record and is not repaired here; item 2 of that decision own judgement queue asks whether attributed debt should gate anything.

No check measures bindings/sov/profile.json governing_sources against the list AGENTS.md owns. scripts/sov_precedent.py asserts only that CONTRACT.md and ENGINEERING.md appear. The drift closed here was unmeasured and can reopen unmeasured.

Identifier collision is a live and unmeasured hazard. This concern lost a commit message to an A20 collision. Seam S26 has already collided and nobody has noticed: origin/claude/federation-architecture-redesign-hkaltp carries S26 as one seam and the main checkout carries S26 as a different one. main and feat/federation-harness-and-hardening have each minted decisions/0093 and 0094 with different content. No check detects a packet-id or seam-id collision across refs: scripts/sovaccept/packet.py tests only whether an id already sits in acceptance/accepted/ in the current tree, and scripts/sovaccept/policy.py tests only that a packet id matches its STATUS.yaml queue entry. Decision numbers have scripts/sov_session.py reserve-decision; packet ids and seam ids have nothing. A21 and S28 were verified free across every local branch, every remote-tracking ref, every rescue ref and the working trees of all live worktrees, by hand, at the time of writing.

scripts/sov_land.py pin is committed on no ref while decisions/0098 instructs witnesses to use it to produce observed_files. It exists only in the uncommitted working tree of the main checkout, so it passes in the one tree that holds it. Every observation on this concern pinned digests by hand instead. Pre-existing and outside this concern.

Per-check budget debt does not reproduce as a stable figure and this packet earlier stated it as though it did. Readings across this branch and main range from five to six checks over ceiling and from 27.060s to 47.183s above budget. Every over-ceiling check is pre-existing on main and unrelated to a documentation change; the spread is the same host-load effect residual 4 records, and stating a load-dependent quantity as a fixed range was the error.

This change touches five paths that grant:standing-landing-loop excludes by name - AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SOV.md, STATUS.yaml and OPEN-SEAMS.md - and four more in no admitted prefix: CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, .cursorrules and acceptance/. The standing landing loop cannot merge this, which is why it is presented rather than landed.
on_accept: Merge docs/plane-separation-entry-points into main. Every launched agent then reads a governing set that names the product plane, and the two groups become the answer to where a product question is settled. Then decide seam S28, whether the third document class needs a decision record, whether the reading list growing from ten to twelve wants one, whether decisions/0081 thirty-second assertion gets repaired or the ceiling does, and whether packet and seam ids get a reservation command.
on_reject: Delete the branch and refs/backup/plane-separation-pre-rewrite. The seven documents return to main wording and the entry points continue to omit the product plane. Seam S28 stays true either way, since it records an ambiguity in a sentence about the 2026-08-24 acceptance rather than about this change. Nothing else depends on this; no standing moved and no product claim changed.
